section.text: Share storage folders with other users
Share storage folders with other users

changes.oldText: A Share Folder modal opens. In the Invite User section, enter User B's email address and select the desired permission level from the Permission dropdown. If you choose Read only, User B will be able to only view the folder but not modify it. If you select Read & Write, User B will be able to both view and modify the folder. Click the Add button to send the invitation.

section.text: Share storage folders with other users

changes.newText: A Share Folder modal opens. In the Invite User section, select User B in the user selector, set Share permission and Mount Permission, then click Invite. Share permission is what the share lets the user do with the folder, and Mount Permission is how the folder is mounted into the user's sessions. An address that does not have an account yet is invited with Invite by e-mail.

changes.oldText: Go to the Data page and check that the tests folder is displayed in the list. If you don't see it on the list, try refreshing your browser page. Since you have accepted the invitation, you can now view the contents of User A's tests folder in User B account. Unlike folders created by User B, the shared folder shows User A's email address in the Owner column. You can also see the Read only mark displayed in the Mount Permission column.

changes.oldText: You can modify the permissions of shared users from the Share Folder modal. The Shared Users section displays a table listing all users who have accepted the invitation. Each row shows the invitee's email address and a permission dropdown. Click the permission dropdown in a user's row to change their access level:
changes.newText: You can modify the permissions of shared users from the Share Folder modal. The Shared Users table lists both the users who have accepted the invitation and the invitations that are still waiting for an answer. Change a listed user's Share permission or Mount Permission in their row.

changes.oldText: Read only: The invited user has read-only access to the folder.
changes.oldHtml: Read only: The invited user has read-only access to the folder.

changes.oldText: Read & Write: The invited user has read and write access to the folder, including creating, modifying, and deleting files and folders within it.

changes.newText: The Folder Info section of the modal shows the folder's Default mount permission. Click Edit to change it.

changes.oldText: To stop sharing a folder as the inviter, open the Share Folder modal by clicking the share button next to the folder's name in the folder list. In the Shared Users table, click the stop sharing icon (red close circle) next to the permission dropdown in the row of the user you want to remove. A confirmation dialog will appear asking you to confirm. Click Confirm to revoke the user's access.
changes.newText: To stop sharing a folder as the inviter, open the Share Folder modal by clicking the share button next to the folder's name in the folder list. In the Shared Users table, click the Stop sharing action in the row of the user you want to remove. A confirmation dialog will appear asking you to confirm. Click Confirm to revoke the user's access. An invitation that is still waiting for an answer is withdrawn with Cancel invitation instead.
